summary: Round 11 plan check, 26 Sep ~17:05-17:25 UTC. (1) All round-10 actions are on main: origin/main is df6996e, every listed CONTEXT entry sits above '## 9. Literature', `python -m pytest -q tests` gives 275 passed, the finals sha values are unchanged (1f1ddb6d, 55038fd6, a77bcd6b) and the claude grep prints 0. (2) The E10 P1 check at 17:01Z shows no kernel or status change against 16:20Z and E10 is not met. amanatar v10 is ERROR, so it has no score. The newest run (anhadmahajan06, 16:17Z) is a clean-room rewrite with a PP sweep on train stems, so it fails P3. API SELECTED is 2/2 at 17:09Z and the poll.log header was 17:06Z. (3) The successor scenario, measured: the builder's divinsert, safetail and lowrefine patches apply to real x138 descendants (amanatar v10 and its older version). Each anchor appears exactly once, the cells compile, and the patch delta is identical to the K1 delta on x138 except for one preset-dict line. So 'successor + insertion' (S+ins) needs only a small builder change. What blocks it is the rules, not the code. P6 bars it as 'new code after R8'. R8 ends consolidation builds at 28 Sep 12:00. R4, P6 and f2 give different answers for a successor at 0.954 or 0.955. So an E10 v2 rule is valid only if it meets four conditions: (a) its code, tests and text are in git before 27 Sep 12:00 UTC; (b) the user's OK is logged before any qualifying successor is seen; (c) it explicitly amends P6, the R8 consolidation cutoff and the 'S12/S13 empty' line; (d) it states which rule takes precedence. A principled threshold is S >= 0.955, i.e. x138 + 0.002 by R4, because S+ins keeps our insertion and only S's own mechanism needs proof. At 0.954 the default is notify only, and the user can opt in with a separate OK. Recommended build: exactly the K1 command on S, which gives C01, R5(a) at 9.5 h and the 8.0 h insertion gate with no §f(iii) waiver. Recommended pair: {S+ins, K2 #37}. The explicit loss case is insertion < 0 AND X_S <= X, about 5-7%. Also missing: a ledger token (exp63* maps to the 7.5 h x138 family), S-specific dummy gates, a night-autonomy clause and the wake mechanism.

findings.what: THRESHOLD AND PAIR for E10 v2. S+ins keeps our insertion, so only S's own mechanism needs R4 proof, and R4 applies against S's real base, x138 (0.953). S >= 0.955 therefore meets R4's +0.002. That makes 0.955 the principled trigger, with no new rule needed. S = 0.954 (x138 + 0.001) does not meet R4. There: notify the user, record it as info, and act only with a separate explicit [OK] item. The pair should be {S+ins, K2 #37}; the twin leaves. Loss case: insertion effect I < 0 AND X_S <= X (x138 private), roughly (0.10-0.15) x (0.4-0.5) = 5-7%. Then both finals sit below the x138 copy block. Win case: X_S > X while S copies land above us, about 0.5-0.6 conditional on a genuine S. Alternatives: {K2, S verbatim} loses to the S copy block on ties, because ties go to the earlier submission. {S+ins, twin} gives up the insertion's upside when X_S <= X.

Copy rate: 0.953 block 241 (25 Sep 13:38) -> 354 (26 Sep 17:01), ~100/day and rising. An S seen on 27 Sep could gather ~150-250 copies by the deadline, enough to move the bronze line past us if X_S > our private.
findings.action: Adopt row (pre-register): S+ins replaces the twin, pair {S+ins, #37}, iff ALL of: (i) S passes tools/e10_port_gate.py (P3/P4b/P4c) on the S verbatim dummy; (ii) S's own page score is >= 0.955 on the pulled latest version; (iii) the S+ins build passes PC11-04 and PC11-09; (iv) S+ins scores without error with R5(a) L_hi <= 9.5 h; (v) S+ins public >= S's page score and >= 0.954. If any fails: the pair stays {#37, #38}, and at S >= 0.956 P6 applies as written. When S >= 0.956, submit S verbatim and S+ins together (2 slots). Pick {S+ins, #37} if (iv)-(v) hold, else {S, #37} by P6. Put the 0.954 opt-in as a separate [OK] line with the 5-7% loss case spelled out.

A gross deviation means S already changes divisions, so no S+ins. 'DIVINS ENABLED: 1 DaughterNet model' must appear in the D2 log.
